title: V2.4.0 PDT-SAFE EXECUTION MODE — a PDT-immune option for accounts under $25,000, chosen at install
summary: NEW OPT-IN EXECUTION MODE (not a signal-logic change). The standard bot places real broker GTC stops plus a resting intraday short-TP1 limit from the moment of entry — great for tight, intraday fills, but those broker orders CAN fill the SAME day as entry. A same-day round trip is a 'day trade', and a MARGIN account under $25,000 making 4+ day trades in 5 business days gets flagged as a Pattern Day Trader (PDT) by FINRA/Alpaca and can be RESTRICTED from day trading. SID takes SHORT trades, and shorting requires a margin account — so a sub-$25K SID account is PDT-subject. v2.4.0 restores the old v2.0 PDT-immune design as an OPT-IN mode. Set SID_PDT_SAFE=true and the bot places NO broker order that can fire intraday: it skips the resting GTC stop, skips the resting intraday short-TP1 limit, and skips the entry-time broker stop — for BOTH the normal entry path and the Telegram-approved entry path. PDT-safe positions are then managed SOLELY by the once-a-day poll (TP1 at RSI-50, TP2 on the 50/200-day SMA, break-even, or the 30-day timeout, and a stop breach → market close at the NEXT day's open). Because the daily poll only ever acts a day or more after entry and there are no broker orders at the exchange, no position can open and close on the same calendar day → it cannot trigger the PDT rule, so a sub-$25K account won't get locked out. HONEST TRADE-OFFS (stated plainly, they're inherent to being PDT-immune): there is no intraday stop, so a hard mid-day move against you isn't cut until the next run's open (gap/slippage), and you should expect a MODEST hit to profitability — on the order of a few percent — versus the standard PDT version; also a missed scheduled run leaves a position unmanaged for longer (no broker safety-net order). DEFAULT is FALSE = the standard PDT version (unchanged), so nothing changes for existing $25K+ setups. The fresh installer (SID-DEPLOY-PROMPT.md) now ASKS your funding size and recommends the mode: $25,000+ → PDT version (best fills, but you must keep the account above $25,000 at all times); under $25,000 → PDT-safe mode. This is not financial advice — you are responsible for your account type and Alpaca's/FINRA's rules. NO canon rule change — RSI 30/70, MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier 80-ticker universe are all untouched, so the headline backtest numbers are unchanged. New: CONFIG.pdtSafe (env SID_PDT_SAFE) + executor.openEntryNoStop(); sid.yml + sid-approve-trade.yml pass SID_PDT_SAFE through.

title: ONE-CLICK FOLLOWER UPDATER — 'Update SID to latest' Action + HOW-TO-UPDATE guide (no clone, no commands, no Claude)
summary: Updating your fork to a new SID version is now a single button. NEW: an 'Update SID to latest' GitHub Action (.github/workflows/sid-update.yml) that you run from your fork's Actions tab — the same tab you already use to run the bot. It pulls the latest strategy CODE + release notes from the source repo and commits them to your fork for you: no local clone, no git commands, no downloads, no Claude. WHICH FILES IT UPDATES lives in ONE place — a plain-text manifest (SID/.sid-update-manifest.txt, self-updating so the updater updates itself) that both the button and the guided update prompt read, so the list can never drift. SAFETY (the guarantee your trades can't be overwritten): after pulling the code, the workflow checks the staged changes against a denylist of every state file — open/closed positions, account ledger, trade log, run log, pending approvals, scanner output, dashboard build output — and if any of them would change it ABORTS before committing or pushing and leaves you exactly as you were. On success it writes a friendly summary with the new version, a one-line what-changed, and in bold: your positions, account balance, trades, and secrets were NOT touched — only the strategy code and release notes were updated. If there's nothing new it just says you're already up to date. A dead-simple, jargon-free guide (SID/HOW-TO-UPDATE.md) walks non-technical followers through it as five numbered clicks, and the deploy + update docs now point at the button as the primary method (the Claude-based SID-UPDATE-PROMPT.md is kept as the advanced/manual fallback). This is tooling only — NO strategy change: RSI 30/70, MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier 80-ticker universe are all untouched, and the strategy version is unchanged at v2.3.0.

title: V2.3.0 TELEGRAM YES/NO TRADE-APPROVAL FLOW — Approve/Skip buttons turn a gated short into a TRACKED bot position
summary: NEW CAPABILITY (not a signal-logic change). Since v2.2.4, a mechanical SHORT on a long-term-bullish asset is gated for your approval — but 'approve' meant manually running sid-manual-trade.yml, which creates an UNTRACKED off-strategy trade with no TP1/TP2 management. v2.3.0 closes that gap. The short-approval Telegram alert now carries [✅ Approve] [❌ Skip] inline buttons. Tapping Approve triggers a Cloudflare Worker which dispatches a new GitHub workflow (sid-approve-trade.yml) that enters the trade as a PROPERLY TRACKED bot position — full TP1 (RSI-50 partial) and TP2 (SMA50/SMA200/BE/timeout) management by the normal bot. HOW APPROVED TRADES BECOME TRACKED: both the bot's normal entry path and the approval path now build the open-positions record through ONE shared factory (buildEntryPositionRecord), so the v2.2.x schema (shares_total/shares_remaining/orig_stop/tp1_hit/brokerStopOrderId/clientOrderIdPrefix/strategy) can never drift — and because the approved position gets a broker GTC stop at entry, checkPositions/maintainV2_2BrokerOrders manage it exactly like an auto-fired one. APPROVE-DAYS-LATER HANDLING: you approve when price reaches your level (e.g. UNH into 439-440), which can be days after the mechanical signal — so approve-trade.js enters at the CURRENT market fill price, recomputes the stop from the current setup (reusing the original level if still valid), sizes by 1% risk on the live entry→stop distance, and logs the proposed-vs-actual entry delta (flagging if it's >5% off). SECURITY (baked in everywhere): only your Telegram chat-id can approve (allowlist), the webhook requires a secret-token header, the GitHub token is fine-grained least-privilege (Actions read+write on ONLY the BotTrading repo), no secrets live in code or the repo (wrangler secret put + repo secrets), it fires on PAPER (SID_TRADING_MODE), and the workflow aborts safely if the approval id is unknown/stale/already-actioned (no blind trade). New pending queue: pending-approvals-sid.json (deterministic id symbol-signalDate-side, de-duped, pruned after 5 days). New files: SID/approve-trade.js, SID/approval-worker/ (worker.js + wrangler.toml + README setup guide), .github/workflows/sid-approve-trade.yml. NO canon rule change — RSI 30/70, MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier 80-ticker universe are all untouched, so the headline backtest numbers are unchanged.

title: V2.2.6 TP2 CANCEL-FIRST FIX — TP2 runner-close no longer fails silently; position cap raised 3→5; BITF removed
summary: LIVE BUG FIXED — the exact twin of the v2.2.5 TP1 bug, on the TP2 branch. After TP1 banks, the v2.2 broker design leaves a full-RUNNER break-even GTC stop resting on Alpaca, and Alpaca 'holds' the runner shares against it — so when checkPositions Branch B fired a TP2 exit and called the full close (DELETE /v2/positions/SYM), it returned `insufficient qty available for order (requested: N, available: 0)` on EVERY run. The old catch just logged tp2_close_fail and re-queued the position, so it retried silently: PYPL (12-share runner, BE $41.41) failed 4x and ADBE (2-share runner, BE $200.79) 2x over 2026-07-13 to 07-16. IMPORTANT — the TP2 trigger itself was LEGITIMATE, not a false positive: both runners had rallied FAVOURABLY up through their 50-day SMA (PYPL last close $56.73 vs SMA50 $44.51 & SMA200 $52.90; ADBE last close $235.31 vs SMA50 $230.94), so the SMA50-touch TP2 fired correctly — they were stuck only because the CLOSE couldn't land while the BE stop held the shares. FIX (mirrors the v2.2.5 TP1 order of operations): (1) CANCEL the resting BE stop first (+ any lingering -stop) and wait for zero open orders to release the runner shares, (2) submit the runner close and POLL that it fills, (3) TP2 fully closes the runner so no re-stop on success — but on a rejected or unconfirmed close the runner is re-protected with a stop, tp2Hit is NOT booked (so it retries next run), and a LOUD Telegram alarm fires (tg.alertTp2CloseFailed). The sid-log tp2_close_fail entry now records the TP2 reason + protection state. ALSO in this release: the concurrent-position cap was raised from 3 to 5 (CONFIG.maxOpenPositions, env SID_MAX_POSITIONS; at the 10% per-position cap that's ~50% of the account max deployed, and 1%-risk sizing is usually well under the cap so real deployment is lower). AND: BITF was removed from the universe — it had been delisted and returned Alpaca HTTP 404 every run, so it was silently skipped; the AUTO-80 tier is unchanged (BITF was HUMAN/log-only, never auto-fired), the universe drops 113→112 and the HUMAN tier 33→32. The stale UNH one-shot close workflow was also deleted (the UNH short it targeted stopped out on its broker stop on 2026-07-01). NO signal-logic change — RSI 30/70, MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier 80-ticker universe are all untouched, so the headline backtest numbers are unchanged.

title: V2.2.5 TP1 CANCEL-FIRST FIX — TP1 partial close no longer fails silently; exit targets now on every card
summary: LIVE BUG FIXED: the long TP1 partial close had been FAILING on every run since 2026-06-26 — PYPL (long 23sh @ $41.395) has had daily RSI(14) at/above 50 the whole time, so TP1 SHOULD have banked, but the close returned `insufficient qty available for order (requested: 11, available: 0)` for FIVE straight days, silently. ROOT CAUSE: the v2.2 broker design leaves a full-size resting GTC stop from entry, and Alpaca 'holds' every share against it, so the DELETE-by-qty partial close can never claim shares. This is the live analogue of the documented Alpaca held-shares/OCO trap. FIX (correct order of operations): when TP1 fires, (1) CANCEL the resting broker stop first to release the shares and wait for them to free, (2) submit the partial close and POLL that it actually fills, (3) only then re-place the break-even stop on the RUNNER (remaining shares) at the direction-aware BE price. If the partial fill is NOT confirmed, the FULL remaining qty is re-protected with a stop so the position is never left naked. The short-side twin was fixed too: while TP1 is pending the resting stop now reserves only the runner half (so the resting TP1 limit can actually be placed — it used to fail the same way), and the TP1 half is placed as an OCO (limit + stop) so both legs are protected. Any TP1 close failure now fires a LOUD Telegram alarm (tg.alertTp1CloseFailed) so a multi-day silent failure can't recur. For PYPL specifically the very next run that sees RSI ≥ 50 will cleanly book the 11-share TP1 and set the $41.41 BE stop on the remaining 12. ALSO (dashboard, Alan-requested): each OPEN-position card now shows the DYNAMIC exit targets so the exits are always visible — TP1 (current daily RSI(14) vs 50 + whether it's banked; for shorts the RSI-50 target price too), TP2 (daily SMA50 and SMA200 runner exits), and the current stop/BE. NO signal-logic change — RSI 30/70, MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier universe are all untouched, so the headline backtest numbers are unchanged. New executor helpers: cancelOrderById / waitForNoOpenOrders / pollOrderFill / placeStop.

title: V2.2.4 SHORT APPROVAL GATE — bullish-asset shorts no longer auto-fire; they need your approval
summary: v2.2.2's MANUAL-WATCH flag only FLAGGED bullish-asset shorts for post-TP1 runner review — it did not block entry. So on 2026-06-30 UNH auto-shorted at $416.52, far below the 439-440 supply zone we actually wanted. v2.2.4 turns that post-entry flag into a PRE-ENTRY APPROVAL GATE: a mechanical SHORT signal on a long-term-bullish asset (price > 200-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA) is no longer auto-executed. The bot logs a short_approval_required entry and sends a Telegram alert (symbol, signal date, current price, proposed entry + stop, would-be size) so Alan can fire it manually at the right level — e.g. into a supply zone — via the existing manual one-shot flow (sid-manual-trade.yml / manual-trade.js). No auto-fire, no reply-to-approve infra for v1. IMPORTANT — this is a LIVE execution-discipline overlay, NOT a signal-logic change: RSI 30/70 thresholds, RSI+MACD alignment, the RSI-50 TP1 trigger, the 14-day earnings blackout and the AUTO-tier 80-ticker universe are ALL untouched. The v2.2.3 backtest (280 trades / 73.9% WR / PF 3.19 / +$31,426, tier1 5y $200 fixed) INCLUDES these bullish-asset shorts firing mechanically — so live results will deliberately DIVERGE from the pure backtest on this subset. The headline backtest numbers are unchanged for exactly that reason. Longs and non-bullish-asset shorts are UNAFFECTED and still auto-fire. Toggle: SID_SHORT_APPROVAL_GATE=false reverts to fully-mechanical bullish-asset shorts. The v2.2.1-era Pine visualiser already distinguishes green=mechanical / amber=manual-watch; that amber flag now corresponds to 'approval-required, not auto-fired.' New: CONFIG.shortApprovalGate + tg.alertShortApprovalNeeded() in bot-sid.js/telegram-alerts.js.

title: V2.2.3 ENTRY OVERHAUL — bot entry realigned to the validated backtest + shorts-only re-arm cooldown
summary: The live bot's entry had silently drifted loose from the validated strategy: it had NO arm timeout, NO RSI(3) confirmation, and NO weekly-SMA arm gate — so it was taking stale, low-quality signals the backtest never measured (caught via a live ADBE long entered 6 trading days after its oversold signal, after price had already slid $233->$202). A bot-parity backtest quantified the drift: the loose live model ran at 66.1% WR / PF 1.91 vs the validated 71.0% / PF 2.69. The fix restores all three gates AND adds an Alan refinement found by sweep: a SHORTS-ONLY 5-day re-arm cooldown (longs re-arm freely to catch bullish V-shaped recoveries; shorts wait out the recovery so they don't re-fire low-quality counter-trend repeats). The short cooldown has a clean optimum at 5 days (short WR 62.9% -> 72.3%; falls off at 3 and 7). Final config: 3-day arm timeout + RSI(3) + weekly SMA50/200 gate + free-rearm longs / shorts-only 5-day cooldown = 280 trades, 73.9% WR, PF 3.19, +$31,426 — Pareto-dominates v2.2.1 (+$2,091, +0.50 PF, +2.9pp WR) with the short side cleaned up. detectEntrySignal was rewritten as a faithful bar-by-bar replay of the validated arm machine; the scan data fetch was bumped 2y->5y so the weekly-SMA gate (needs ~200 weekly bars) actually applies live. Verified: reproduces the backtest's entries exactly (GOOG, AAPL), and the stale ADBE entry no longer fires. Exit logic (v2.2.1 hybrid TP1/TP2, broker stops) and the v2.2.2 MANUAL-WATCH flag are unchanged. Full investigation: SID/strategy-test-vault/bot-parity-experiment/.

title: MANUAL-WATCH flag (v2.2.2) — bullish-asset short runners flagged for S/R review
summary: No change to how trades fire — a monitoring aid on top of v2.2.1. The bot now flags any open SHORT on a long-term-bullish asset (price > 200-day SMA AND 50-day SMA > 200-day SMA) as MANUAL-WATCH, because on those names the mechanical TP2 has a blind spot: RSI rarely reaches daily oversold before the bounce, and the SMA exit can round-trip to break-even (30% of runners do). Proven by the GOOG 2026-06 trade (runner RSI bottomed at 38.4, never near oversold) and the TP2-RSI experiment (rsi_oversold fired only 6 times across 89 shorts; replacing the SMA exit with RSI-extreme DOUBLED round-trips to BE — rejected). The flag now shows as a pulsing 👁 WATCH · S/R badge on the dashboard position card, prints a ⚠ MANUAL-WATCH line in the bot log, and sends a consolidated Telegram reminder each run. TP1 still banks mechanically; only the runner half needs the eye. Helper: longTermBullish() in bot-sid.js. Catalogue: SID/strategy-test-vault/tp2-rsi-experiment/.

title: V2.2.1 HYBRID launch — broker-managed stops, side-asymmetric TP1 timing
summary: Per-side decomposition of v2.2 revealed an asymmetry: shorts strictly benefit from intraday-touch TP1 (higher WR AND higher PnL), but longs lose $2.3k over 5y because the bullish drift of US equities WORKS FOR longs — letting price close past RSI 50 books a bigger TP1 partial than locking exactly at 50. V2.2.1 routes by side: longs use v2.1 close-based TP1 (RSI ≥ 50 on daily close), shorts use v2.2 intraday-touch TP1 (resting GTC limit at the RSI-50 target price computed via Wilder-RSI inversion). Both sides keep a broker-enforced GTC stop on Alpaca from the moment of entry — replaces v2.1's PDT-immune 'scan daily candle, close at next open' simulation. Sizing now compounds off the internal $9,351.16 ledger (1% risk = $93.51). Backtest gate (tier1, 5y, $200 fixed risk): WR 69.6% → 71.3% (+1.7pp), PF 2.62 → 2.72 (+0.10), Total PnL $29,317 → $29,528 (+$211). Hybrid Pareto-dominates v2.1 on every metric AND recovers $2,163 of the PnL pure v2.2 left on the table. First v2.2.1 entry (PYPL long, 23sh @ $41.40, signal 2026-06-05) opened 2026-06-12. Vault: SID/strategy-test-vault/v2.2.1-hybrid-shorts-intraday/.

title: BE stop direction-aware penny rounding — no more small-loss BE exits
summary: bot-sid.js:931 used Math.round(entry) for the post-TP1 BE stop, which was direction-blind — a long entry of $281.49 rounded DOWN to $281 (tiny loss locked in), and a short entry of $381.84 rounded UP to $382 (tiny loss locked in). Replaced with direction-aware penny rounding: long stop = entry+0.01, short stop = entry−0.01. Every BE stop now locks in ≥1¢/share profit instead of risking a small loss. Existing GOOG position retrofitted from $382 → $381.83. Audit task #11 MED finding resolved.

summary: RSI overbought (73.12) episode from 2026-04-17, trigger fired May 26 with RSI 58.1 + MACD both pointing down. Stop $405 (Math.ceil of episode high). Position currently flat, working as designed.

title: manual-trade.js: OCO + safety fallback pattern
summary: Original pattern (TP1 limit + standalone SL) was rejected by Alpaca with 'insufficient qty' because TP1 held half the shares. Now uses OCO bracket for the TP1 half + standalone stop for the runner. Safety fallback places full-position stop if OCO fails. Telegram alerts added.

title: Pine tp2*Be branches now explicitly close
summary: BE stop after TP1 was ghosting on Pine v6, leaving positions stuck IN-RUNNER forever (tp2Hit=true blocked all other exits — irrecoverable deadlock). Mirror the SMA50/200/Timeout pattern: cancel BE + strategy.close + flag.

title: GHA cron one-shot pattern replaces local scheduler
summary: Manual trades now fire from GitHub runners via cron with date-guards, not via Claude Code's local scheduled-tasks (which required PC to be on). Cloud-first architecture restored.

title: Pine pitfall catalog established
summary: Root CLAUDE.md now hosts a cross-strategy Pine bug catalog (10 entries) with back-refs to detailed write-ups in each strategy's memory. Memory-update convention requires any new Pine fix to append a row here.

title: First live paper trade: GOOG short fired
summary: Regular bot run picked up GOOG short (26sh @ $381.84, stop $405). 9-day signal-to-entry episode with the May 18 $404.47 high becoming the stop. PDT-immune by design — bot manages stops internally.

title: Pine info table now renders on 1D
summary: barstate.islast was not firing on UNH 1D (worked on 4h). Broadened gate to barstate.islast OR barstate.islastconfirmedhistory OR bar_index >= last_bar_index - 1. Confirmed via data_get_pine_tables MCP query.

title: Pine three-layer safety force-close
summary: Stuck-runner positions opened before the entryBarIdx variable existed had it as na, so the 90-bar safety check never fired. Now triple-layer: init entryBarIdx if na + safety on barsSinceEntry + safety on barsSinceTp1.

title: bot-sid.js scan path: 6mo → 2y daily lookback
summary: Default fetchDailyCandles range was 6mo (~125-130 daily bars → ~26-28 weekly bars after resample, below the 30-bar minimum for the weekly check). 9 AUTO-tier tickers were silently rejected with 'insufficient weekly history'. Fix: explicit '2y' on the scan path.

title: Pine strategy.close() blocked by pending strategy.exit()
summary: After TP1 set a BE stop via strategy.exit, the BE order hung on the entry and blocked all subsequent strategy.close() calls — positions stuck IN RUNNER from decades ago, locking the strategy slot. Fix: cancel BE exit BEFORE every strategy.close() in TP2 branches.

title: V2.1 Dynamic TP1+TP2 launch (paper)
summary: Two-stage exit: TP1 closes 50% at RSI 50 and moves stop to break-even; TP2 closes runner on BE / SMA50 / SMA200 / 30-bar timeout. Backtest: 302 trades, 69.5% WR, PF 2.55, +$28k over 5y at fixed $200 risk. v2.0 single-exit toggle preserved (SID_DYNAMIC_TP=false).

title: V2.1 backtest warmup bug fixed
summary: main() was downloading only 5y of price data — Wilder RSI and weekly resamples weren't seasoned at the start of the trade window, silently rejecting ~75% of signals in years 1-3. Now downloads HISTORY_WARMUP_DAYS + BACKTEST_YEARS, filters trades after warmup ends.
